# Drafts (Workflow and Timeline series, spec 1) Implementation Plan

> **Release branch (owner, 2026-10-04):** `release/workflow-graph`, cut from `origin/release/knowledge-graph` at f9e0cd18. Every task branch is cut from `origin/release/workflow-graph` and every PR goes `--base release/workflow-graph`. The Knowledge Graph release merges to `main` first; `main` is then merged INTO `release/workflow-graph`, never rebased.

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking. In the gisik orchestration, every task is ONE lane session. Follow `gisik-nokma-lanes/STEPS-common-2026-10-03.md`: numbered steps, each ending with a pushed commit + `CHECKPOINT task/<branch> <sha40> step <n>/<N>` + `HANDOFF-<branch>.md`; the sweep list + your own mutation pass before DONE.

**Goal:** a ticket can be created as a private DRAFT (no key, no board, no list, no search, no notice, visible to its author alone, the owner and the assignee included), kept on a Drafts page, given attachments, published (it takes the next key and lands at the END of its project's Backlog) or discarded (erased now, with the attachments uploaded from it), singly or as an atomic ordered set, from the app, offline and from MCP.

**Architecture:**
- **A draft is a ticket with a flag** (spec D1): `ticket.created {draft:true}` births it, `ticket.published {projectId}` and `ticket.discarded {}` end the state. `TicketState.draft` folds in the one shared reducer, so the server, the replica and the fixtures agree.
- **Privacy is one flag closed in four shared places** (spec §4.1): `proj_visibility.draft_author_id` and `proj_tickets.draft_author_id`; `canSeeResolved`/`canSee` answer false for everyone, the author included; `visibleTicketsWhere` and `LIVE_TICKET_WHERE` AND `draft_author_id IS NULL`. The author reaches a draft only through eleven named doors that call `canOpen`/`ticketAccess` (`visibility/can-open.ts`). A census test (28.050) fails on any `proj_tickets`/`proj_visibility` SQL or `canSee(` call that is in no group.
- **Keys are counted from the publish event** (spec §6): the key query counts `ticket.created` rows that are not drafts plus `ticket.published` rows, and the purge keeps both, redacted.
- **Atomic publish** is one new ingest primitive (`commitInTx`, `ingestAtomic`) and one online route; links that touch a draft live on the draft's own stream (an additive `from` member on spec A's link payloads) until publish re-files them in the same transaction.

**Tech stack:** TypeScript, zod 3, Postgres (node-pg-migrate SQL files), Fastify, React 19, Next (apps/web), better-sqlite3 (replica tests), vitest 3 (node + jsdom), Playwright is NOT used here.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-03-drafts-design.md`. Read it first; its section numbers (§) and requirement ids (R1–R66) are cited below. Code was read at `origin/release/knowledge-graph` (`ec72d1f8`: it carries typed-links T1 and the KG catalogue seed). **Every `file:line` below is from that tree; typed-links T2-T5 and the rest of the KG series land BEFORE this plan runs, so re-read each file at the cut of the new release branch before editing it** (the places that will have moved are named in each task).

**Model facts, copied from the spec**
- **Events** (all against entity kind `ticket`, version 1; `ENTITY_KINDS` does not change, `packages/domain/test/envelope.test.ts:310`):
  - `ticket.created` gains `draft: z.literal(true).optional()`; absent means published at birth (what every stored event meant). A second `.refine`: `draft === true ⇒ start === 'backlog' AND stateId === undefined`, message `a draft is born in the backlog: send start: "backlog" and no stateId`.
  - `ticket.published` payload `{ projectId: ulidString }`, `.strict()`; `ticket.discarded` payload `{}`, `.strict()`.
- **State:** `TicketState.draft?: { authorId: string; at: string; discarded?: true }`, ABSENT on every non-draft. `ticket.published` removes it and re-pins `workflowId`/`workflowVersion` to the type's CURRENT binding (state stays Backlog); `ticket.discarded` sets `draft.discarded = true`.
- **Rules and refusal ids** (dotted `REFUSALS` keys; `REFUSAL_RULES` is kebab and pinned by `packages/rule-engine/test/engine.test.ts:671-702`, never touched):

  | Id | When | Sentence |
  |---|---|---|
  | `draft.not-allowed` | an event outside the author's allowlist (R6/R7) | `A draft cannot be <verb>. Publish it first, or discard it.`; for `ticket.deleted`: `A draft cannot be deleted. Discard it instead.` |
  | `draft.parent-unpublished` | publishing a draft whose parent is an unpublished draft (R11) | the same sentence |
  | `draft.not-a-draft` | `ticket.published`/`ticket.discarded` on a non-draft (R12) | `This ticket is not a draft.` |
  | `draft.project-mismatch` | `ticket.published.projectId` is not the draft's project | `The project does not match this draft's project.` |
  | `draft.no-outsiders` | assign-outsider with a draft event or a draft target (R8) | `Publish the ticket before inviting someone from outside` |
  | `draft.link-form` | a plain `ticket.link_added` on S naming a draft target (R43) | `Link to a draft from the draft's side` |
  | `draft.link-refile-refused` | the publish cannot re-file an incoming link or a pending child (R44) | names the source (or the child) and the cause |

  Owner ruling O1 (2026-10-04) removed `draft.parent-is-draft`: a published ticket's own stream naming any draft as parent is answered `hierarchy.unknown-parent` (to anyone but its author a draft id is not a ticket), and a draft parent for a published ticket is filed from the DRAFT's side (`ticket.reparented {newParentId: D, childId: C}` on D's stream, T6, spec R4).
  | `draft.publish-refused` | the atomic route's 409 body (R49) | `{ rule, ticketId, cause: { rule, reason } }` |
  | `hierarchy.unknown-parent` | another person's draft named as parent (R3) | the existing sentence (no oracle) |
  | `permission.visibility` | anyone else touching a draft (R9) | `TICKET_NOT_VISIBLE_REASON` |
  | `ticket.unknown` | a discarded draft (R12) | the existing sentence |
- **Author's allowlist (R6):** `ticket.field_set`, `ticket.assigned`, `ticket.reparented`, `ticket.link_added`, `ticket.link_removed`, `attachment.added`, `ticket.published`, `ticket.discarded` (and, on the NOTE's stream, `note.attached`/`note.detached` naming the draft, R66). Everything else refused (R7); comments open after publish.
- **Audience (R17/R18):** exactly the author, only while they hold owner/admin/member and the project is in `eff.projects`. The visibility-controls disclosure text must say drafts are the exception.
- **Keys (R25/R26):** a ticket's number is its position per project among `ticket.created` rows whose payload does not say `draft: true` plus `ticket.published` rows, ordered by `workspace_seq`. Purge keeps both (`{projectId, purged: true}` plus `draft: true` on a redacted draft creation).
- **Atomic publish (R47-R55):** `POST /v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/drafts/publish` body `{ ticketIds: string[] }` (1 to 200, ordered, no repeats), online only; success `{ results: [{ ticketId, key }] }`, refusal `409 { rule: 'draft.publish-refused', ticketId, cause: { rule, reason } }`, nothing committed. Order is the caller's.
- **Rank on publish (R64/R65):** publish is `ticket.published` then `ticket.ranked`; the backfill ranks come first; `planTailRank(rows, tailIds)` is shared by the server and the client; only Backlog rows the publisher can see are ranked.
- **Discard (R32-R37, R58-R59):** erase after confirm, through the sanctioned purge path; attachments UPLOADED FROM the draft go (rows and objects); a linked note survives and is only unlinked.
- **Notifications (R31):** drafting is silent; publish sends one `assignment` notice (dedupe `assignment:${env.id}`) and one `mention` notice per mentioned person in the description, never to the publisher.
- **Drafts page (§12.2):** route `apps/web/app/w/[workspaceId]/drafts/page.tsx`, nav entry **Drafts** with a count badge, `GET /v1/workspaces/:id/drafts` → `{ items: [{ ticketId, projectId, projectName, typeId, title, parentId, updatedAt, attachmentCount }] }`, `GET /v1/me/drafts` for MCP. Never a key.

**Copy rules (exact strings; no spaced em dash in any new string literal; the ui-copy scan sweeps `packages/domain/src` and `packages/mcp-server/src`)**
- Dialog: secondary button `Save as draft`; toast `Draft saved` with action `Open`.
- Drafts page: nav `Drafts`; empty state `No drafts. A draft is a ticket only you can see, until you publish it.`; row actions `Publish`, `Discard`.
- Sheet: pill `Draft` (dashed outline, in the key's place); banner `Only you can see this draft.` with `Publish` (primary) and `Discard`; disabled controls say `Available after you publish`.
- Discard confirm: `Discard this draft? It is erased and can't be recovered.`; `N sub-drafts will be erased too`; `N attachments uploaded to this draft will be permanently deleted`; `Linked notes are kept and unlinked.`; button `Discard draft`.
- History: `ticket.created` with `draft` reads `Drafted as <Type>`; `ticket.published` reads `Published`.
- MCP `create_ticket` description adds: `A draft is private to you until publish_draft. It has no key.` `discard_draft` preview: `Erases the draft "<title>", N sub-drafts and M attachments uploaded to them (permanently deleted). Linked notes are kept. This cannot be undone.`

## Review Focus

1. **A path nobody listed.** A later-added read or SQL site that returns a draft to its author's other surfaces or to anyone else (a count, a rollup, a search hit, a notification, the Knowledge Graph). Pinned by the census 28.050 (a planted route is reported), the per-row controls 28.051–28.064 and the rollup/`restrictedCount` cases 28.058–28.059 (T3).
2. **Reconcile purging the author's own draft at catch-up.** It looks like data loss and is the quiet one. Pinned by 28.072 (T4), with a mutation that swaps `canOpen` back to `canSee` at `reconcile-route.ts:153`.
3. **A key consumed or shifted.** A draft takes no number; a discard leaves no gap; purging an unpublished draft, or a published draft-born ticket, must not move any other ticket's number. Pinned by 28.021–28.024 (T2).
4. **A half-applied publish.** A set whose third draft is refused must commit nothing: no `ticket.published` row, no key consumed, no notification, no rank. And a re-file that cannot be made refuses the whole publish. Pinned by 28.103 (T5b) and 28.120–28.124 (T6).
5. **Discard erasing something it did not create.** An attachment on another ticket, a note's own attachment, a linked note. Pinned by 28.183 and 28.185 (T9), with the `objectKeysOf` mutation.

**Order and parallelism**
- **T1 → T2 → T3 → T4 → T5 → T5b**, one after the other: each consumes the previous one's columns, predicates or doors.
- **T6 and T9 after T5b** (T6 adds the `from` form and the publish re-file; T9 adds the rank events and G10), in either order. **T7 after T5b** (it publishes through the atomic route). **T8 after T9** (the app's single publish sends `planTailRank` events) and after T6 (the Links section shows draft-side links).
- **Shared files:** `ticket-state.ts` (T1; T6 edits the three link arms); `commitInTx` in `ingest-service.ts` (T5b creates it, T6 adds the re-file); `check-permission.ts` (T4 G1, T6 the link-form rule, T9 G11); `ingest-service.ts` (T5b, T6 hook); `routes/drafts-publish.ts` (T5b creates it, T9 adds the rank events); `write-tools.ts` (T7). `test-cases/28-drafts.md` and Features §25: the anchors.

**Case ownership exceptions (stated so no id is allocated twice):** 28.102 (discard with an incoming draft-side link) and 28.105 (events/History hide a draft-side link) sit in T5's id range but need the `from` form, so **T6 writes them**. 28.098, 28.099, 28.103 and 28.104 (the atomic route's answers, `ingestAtomic`, atomicity, `commitOne` parity) are **T5b's**. T5's block keeps 28.090–28.097, 28.100, 28.101 and 28.106–28.109.

**Forced changes to the spec's task split (the code is the reason)**
1. **T5 is split into T5 and T5b.** Single publish and discard (rules, fanout, grant trigger, erasure, sweep) are one reviewable change; `ingestAtomic` re-factors the single hot-path writer of the whole ledger (`ingest-service.ts:166` `commitOne`) and wants its own review gate and its own parity case (28.104). Same case block, two ledger rows (`5`, `5b`).
2. **T4 also implements the permission-level allowlist (G1).** Doors that admit the author with no rule behind them would let a draft be transitioned between T4 and T5. T4 refuses non-allowlisted types at G1 (`draft.not-allowed`); T5 adds the engine twin (`checkTicketDraft`) for the client precheck, fixtures and the replica, and owns the full matrix (28.090).
3. **T8 depends on T9** (not the reverse), because the app's publish sends `planTailRank`'s events.
4. **T5 also changes three child-count sites the spec does not list.** A Backlog draft under a published parent counted as an open child in `close.ts:71`, `transition.ts:153` and the auto-close `NOT EXISTS` (`auto-close/sweep.ts:187-193`), so a parent could not be finished over work only its author sees and the refusal's number disclosed the draft. T5 excludes drafts in all three (28.096).
5. **R4 follows owner ruling O1 (2026-10-04).** There is no `draft.parent-is-draft`. A plain-form published ticket naming any draft as parent is `hierarchy.unknown-parent` (T5), and the draft-side relation (`childId` on `ticket.reparented`, filed on the draft's stream, re-filed at publish, erased by discard) is T6's, beside the `from` links (cases 28.128, 28.129).

**Interfaces:**
- **Produces** (from `@gisik-nokma/domain`):
  - `ticketPublishedPayload`, `ticketDiscardedPayload` (zod, strict);
  - `ticketCreatedPayload`'s new optional `draft: true`;
  - `TicketState.draft?: TicketDraft` and `type TicketDraft = { authorId: string; at: string; discarded?: true }`;
  - from `draft.ts`: `isDraft(state: Pick<TicketState, 'draft'>): boolean` (a draft exists, discarded or not), `isDiscardedDraft(state)`, `DRAFT_ALLOWED_EVENT_TYPES`, `DRAFT_GATE_EXEMPT_EVENT_TYPES`, `draftAllows(type: string): boolean`, `draftNotAllowedReason(type: string): string`.
- **Produces** (server): `payloadIds('ticket.published', …)` names the project.
- **Consumed by:** T2 (reducer shape for the rows), T3 (`TicketState.draft` for the column mapping), T5 (`draftAllows`, `draftNotAllowedReason` in the engine twin of the permission gate).

**Why `draft` is absent on every non-draft (and not `undefined`-valued or `null`).** `links` took the same rule (typed-links T1/T2): the dual-client rig compares whole `TicketState`s with `toEqual` (`apps/server/test/dual-client/rig.ts:753`), so the reducer, `rowToTicketState` (T3) and the replica must agree on shape. The reducer therefore never writes the key for a published ticket, and `ticket.published` REMOVES it with a rest-destructure rather than setting it to `undefined` (`toEqual` ignores `undefined` members but `'draft' in state` readers and JSON do not).

**Between T1 and T5 a `ticket.published` or `ticket.discarded` on a ticket that is not a draft would throw in the reducer, inside the ingest transaction.** Nothing emits either until T5's doors exist (the app and MCP arrive in T7/T8), the engine twin arrives in T5, and nothing deploys before the release PR. Same stance as typed-links T1 took for link events with no rules.

  ```ts
  import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
  import {
    applyTicketEvent,
    domainRegistry,
    DRAFT_ALLOWED_EVENT_TYPES,
    DRAFT_GATE_EXEMPT_EVENT_TYPES,
    draftAllows,
    draftNotAllowedReason,
    isDiscardedDraft,
    isDraft,
    makeEnvelope,
    newUlid,
    parseEvent,
    ticketCreatedPayload,
    ticketDiscardedPayload,
    ticketPublishedPayload,
    type EventTypeRegistration,
    type TicketState,
    type TicketStateDeps,
    type TicketTypeDef,
    type WorkflowDef,
  } from '../src/index.js';

  const TICKET = newUlid();
  const PROJECT = newUlid();
  const AUTHOR = '01J9GUKR000000000000000000';
  const AT = '2026-10-03T09:00:00.000Z';

  const wf = (id: string, version: number): WorkflowDef => ({
    id,
    version,
    name: id,
    initialStateId: 'todo',
    states: [{ id: 'todo', name: 'To do', category: 'open' }],
    transitions: [{ from: '*', to: 'todo', rules: [] }],
  });
  const WORKFLOWS = [wf('wf-a', 1), wf('wf-b', 3)];

  /** The type's binding is mutable on purpose: 28.003 re-points it while the ticket is a draft. */
  let boundTo = 'wf-a';
  const deps: TicketStateDeps = {
    getTicketType: (id): TicketTypeDef | undefined =>
      id === 'task' ? { id: 'task', name: 'Task', icon: 'check', rank: 3, workflowId: boundTo, fields: [] } : undefined,
    getWorkflow: (id) => WORKFLOWS.find((w) => w.id === id),
  };

  const created = (extra: Record<string, unknown> = {}) =>
    makeEnvelope({
      type: 'ticket.created',
      entity: { kind: 'ticket', id: TICKET },
      actorId: AUTHOR,
      serverTime: AT,
      payload: { typeId: 'task', projectId: PROJECT, parentId: null, title: 'Plan the launch', ...extra },
    });
  const on = (type: string, payload: unknown = {}) =>
    makeEnvelope({ type, entity: { kind: 'ticket', id: TICKET }, actorId: AUTHOR, payload });

  const draftState = (): TicketState => applyTicketEvent(undefined, created({ start: 'backlog', draft: true }), deps);
  const plainState = (): TicketState => applyTicketEvent(undefined, created({ start: 'backlog' }), deps);

  describe('28.001 the draft member of ticket.created', () => {
    const base = { typeId: 'task', projectId: PROJECT, parentId: null, title: 't' };
    it('28.001 draft needs start backlog and no stateId; the v1 shapes still parse', () => {
      expect(ticketCreatedPayload.safeParse({ ...base, start: 'backlog', draft: true }).success).toBe(true);
      for (const bad of [
        { start: 'focus', draft: true },
        { draft: true },
        { start: 'backlog', stateId: 'doing', draft: true },
        { start: 'backlog', draft: false },
      ]) {
        expect(ticketCreatedPayload.safeParse({ ...base, ...bad }).success, JSON.stringify(bad)).toBe(false);
      }
      const refused = ticketCreatedPayload.safeParse({ ...base, draft: true });
      expect(!refused.success && refused.error.issues[0]?.message).toBe(
        'a draft is born in the backlog: send start: "backlog" and no stateId',
      );
      // control: without `draft` nothing changed
      expect(ticketCreatedPayload.safeParse({ ...base, start: 'focus' }).success).toBe(true);
      expect(ticketCreatedPayload.safeParse({ ...base }).success).toBe(true);
    });
  });

  describe('28.002 ticket.published / ticket.discarded', () => {
    it('28.002 strict payloads; registered at v1 against ticket only; the door admits them on a ticket, not a note', () => {
      expect(ticketPublishedPayload.safeParse({ projectId: PROJECT }).success).toBe(true);
      expect(ticketPublishedPayload.safeParse({ projectId: 'GN' }).success).toBe(false);
      expect(ticketPublishedPayload.safeParse({ projectId: PROJECT, extra: 1 }).success).toBe(false);
      expect(ticketPublishedPayload.safeParse({}).success).toBe(false);
      expect(ticketDiscardedPayload.safeParse({}).success).toBe(true);
      expect(ticketDiscardedPayload.safeParse({ reason: 'x' }).success).toBe(false);
      const keys = domainRegistry.registrations().map((r) => `${r.type}@${r.version}`);
      for (const type of ['ticket.published', 'ticket.discarded']) {
        expect(domainRegistry.get(type, 1)?.entityKind).toBe('ticket');
        expect(keys.filter((k) => k === `${type}@1`)).toHaveLength(1);
      }
      const door = (type: string, payload: unknown, kind: 'ticket' | 'note') => {
        const { serverTime: _s, seq: _q, ...submitted } = makeEnvelope({ type, entity: { kind, id: TICKET }, payload });
        return parseEvent(submitted);
      };
      expect(door('ticket.published', { projectId: PROJECT }, 'ticket').ok).toBe(true); // control
      expect(door('ticket.discarded', {}, 'ticket').ok).toBe(true);
      const onNote = door('ticket.published', { projectId: PROJECT }, 'note');
      expect(!onNote.ok && onNote.code).toBe('entity-kind-mismatch');
      expect(door('ticket.discarded', {}, 'note').ok).toBe(false);
    });
  });

  describe('28.003 the reducer: drafted, then published', () => {
    it('28.003 draft = {authorId, at}; publish clears it and re-pins to the type binding in force NOW; control: a non-draft is unchanged', () => {
      boundTo = 'wf-a';
      const born = draftState();
      expect(born.draft).toEqual({ authorId: AUTHOR, at: AT });
      expect(born.stateId).toBe('backlog');
      expect(born.rank).toBeNull();
      expect(born.workflowId).toBe('wf-a');
      const plain = plainState();
      expect('draft' in plain).toBe(false); // control

      boundTo = 'wf-b'; // the type was re-pointed while the draft sat
      try {
        const published = applyTicketEvent(born, on('ticket.published', { projectId: PROJECT }), deps);
        expect('draft' in published).toBe(false);
        expect(published.workflowId).toBe('wf-b');
        expect(published.workflowVersion).toBe(3);
        expect(published.stateId).toBe('backlog');
        expect(published.stateCategory).toBe('open');
        expect(published.fields['title']?.value).toBe('Plan the launch');
        // control: the ticket that was never a draft stayed on the workflow it was created under
        expect(plain.workflowId).toBe('wf-a');
      } finally {
        boundTo = 'wf-a';
      }
    });
  });

  describe('28.004 discarded, and the arms that throw', () => {
    it('28.004 discard marks the flag and keeps who and when; publish and discard on a non-draft throw', () => {
      const born = draftState();
      expect(isDraft(born)).toBe(true);
      expect(isDiscardedDraft(born)).toBe(false); // control
      const gone = applyTicketEvent(born, on('ticket.discarded'), deps);
      expect(gone.draft).toEqual({ authorId: AUTHOR, at: AT, discarded: true });
      expect(isDraft(gone)).toBe(true);
      expect(isDiscardedDraft(gone)).toBe(true);
      const plain = plainState();
      expect(isDraft(plain)).toBe(false);
      expect(() => applyTicketEvent(plain, on('ticket.published', { projectId: PROJECT }), deps)).toThrow(
        new RegExp(`ticket.published for ticket ${TICKET} that is not a draft`),
      );
      expect(() => applyTicketEvent(plain, on('ticket.discarded'), deps)).toThrow(
        new RegExp(`ticket.discarded for ticket ${TICKET} that is not a draft`),
      );
    });
  });

  const onTicket = (r: EventTypeRegistration) =>
    r.entityKind === 'ticket' || (Array.isArray(r.entityKind) && r.entityKind.includes('ticket'));

  /**
   * The refused side of the partition, written out. A NEW ticket-scoped type is in none of the three lists
   * and the census below reports it: the author decides which side it is on.
   */
  const REFUSED: readonly string[] = [
    'ticket.transitioned',
    'ticket.collaborator_added',
    'ticket.collaborator_removed',
    'ticket.workflow_rebound',
    'ticket.closed',
    'ticket.reopened',
    'ticket.ranked',
    'ticket.deleted',
    'ticket.restored',
    'comment.added',
    'comment.edited',
    'comment.deleted',
    'visibility.set',
  ];

  function unclassified(registrations: readonly EventTypeRegistration[]): string[] {
    const known = new Set<string>([...DRAFT_ALLOWED_EVENT_TYPES, ...DRAFT_GATE_EXEMPT_EVENT_TYPES, ...REFUSED]);
    return registrations.filter((r) => onTicket(r) && !known.has(r.type)).map((r) => r.type);
  }

  describe('28.007 the author allowlist', () => {
    it('28.007 eight allowed, bookkeeping exempt, the rest refused with a sentence that names the way out; the census partitions the registry', () => {
      expect([...DRAFT_ALLOWED_EVENT_TYPES].sort()).toEqual(
        [
          'attachment.added',
          'ticket.assigned',
          'ticket.discarded',
          'ticket.field_set',
          'ticket.link_added',
          'ticket.link_removed',
          'ticket.published',
          'ticket.reparented',
        ].sort(),
      );
      for (const type of DRAFT_ALLOWED_EVENT_TYPES) expect(draftAllows(type), type).toBe(true);
      for (const type of DRAFT_GATE_EXEMPT_EVENT_TYPES) expect(draftAllows(type), type).toBe(true);
      for (const type of REFUSED) {
        expect(draftAllows(type), type).toBe(false);
        expect(draftNotAllowedReason(type), type).toMatch(/^A draft cannot be .+\. Publish it first, or discard it\.$|^A draft cannot be deleted\. Discard it instead\.$/);
      }
      expect(draftNotAllowedReason('ticket.deleted')).toBe('A draft cannot be deleted. Discard it instead.');
      expect(draftNotAllowedReason('ticket.closed')).toBe('A draft cannot be closed. Publish it first, or discard it.');
      expect(draftNotAllowedReason('comment.added')).toBe('A draft cannot be commented on. Publish it first, or discard it.');
      // the census: control first (a planted type is reported), then the registry itself
      const planted = { type: 'ticket.planted_for_census', version: 1, entityKind: 'ticket', payloadSchema: undefined as never } as EventTypeRegistration;
      expect(unclassified([...domainRegistry.registrations(), planted])).toEqual(['ticket.planted_for_census']);
      expect(unclassified(domainRegistry.registrations())).toEqual([]);
      // the three lists are disjoint
      const all = [...DRAFT_ALLOWED_EVENT_TYPES, ...DRAFT_GATE_EXEMPT_EVENT_TYPES, ...REFUSED];
      expect(new Set(all).size).toBe(all.length);
    });
  });
  ```

  ```ts
  import type { TicketState } from './entity-state.js';

  /**
   * What an author may submit on their OWN draft (drafts spec §3.3, R6). Everything else is refused
   * `draft.not-allowed` (R7) — comments, transitions, closing, ranking, deleting, collaborators, visibility.
   * `note.attached` / `note.detached` naming a draft are also allowed, but they are filed on the NOTE's
   * stream, so they are decided by the note-side gate (T9), not by this list.
   */
  export const DRAFT_ALLOWED_EVENT_TYPES = [
    'ticket.field_set',
    'ticket.assigned',
    'ticket.reparented',
    'ticket.link_added',
    'ticket.link_removed',
    'attachment.added',
    'ticket.published',
    'ticket.discarded',
  ] as const;

  /**
   * Ticket-scoped types the draft gate does NOT judge, each for a reason a reader can check: `ticket.created`
   * is the birth, not an act on a draft; the contest pair is the server's record of a refusal (an offline
   * draft edit that was refused must still be recordable); `purge.*` have their own refusals
   * (`checkLifecycle`, `purge/check-purged.ts`).
   */
  export const DRAFT_GATE_EXEMPT_EVENT_TYPES = [
    'ticket.created',
    'claim.contested',
    'claim.contested_resolved',
    'purge.marked',
    'purge.unmarked',
    'purge.completed',
  ] as const;

  const ALLOWED: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(DRAFT_ALLOWED_EVENT_TYPES);
  const EXEMPT: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(DRAFT_GATE_EXEMPT_EVENT_TYPES);

  /** The verb in `A draft cannot be <verb>.` for each refused type; an unlisted type reads `changed that way`. */
  const VERBS: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {
    'ticket.transitioned': 'moved',
    'ticket.closed': 'closed',
    'ticket.reopened': 'reopened',
    'ticket.ranked': 'ranked',
    'ticket.restored': 'restored',
    'ticket.workflow_rebound': 'moved to another workflow',
    'ticket.collaborator_added': 'shared with collaborators',
    'ticket.collaborator_removed': 'shared with collaborators',
    'comment.added': 'commented on',
    'comment.edited': 'commented on',
    'comment.deleted': 'commented on',
    'visibility.set': 'shared',
  };

  /** True when an author may submit this type on their draft (allowlisted or exempt). */
  export function draftAllows(type: string): boolean {
    return ALLOWED.has(type) || EXEMPT.has(type);
  }

  /** The sentence for a refused type: names the way out (spec §3.3, R7). Total: any type gets a sentence. */
  export function draftNotAllowedReason(type: string): string {
    if (type === 'ticket.deleted') return 'A draft cannot be deleted. Discard it instead.';
    return `A draft cannot be ${VERBS[type] ?? 'changed that way'}. Publish it first, or discard it.`;
  }

  /** A draft exists on this state, discarded or not. A published ticket has no `draft` key. */
  export function isDraft(state: Pick<TicketState, 'draft'>): boolean {
    return state.draft !== undefined;
  }

  /** The author has discarded it: every door treats it as gone until the erasure lands. */
  export function isDiscardedDraft(state: Pick<TicketState, 'draft'>): boolean {
    return state.draft?.discarded === true;
  }
  ```

**Interfaces:**
- **Consumes** (T1): `ticketPublishedPayload`; the `draft` member on `ticket.created`.
- **Produces** (domain): `redactedTicketCreatedPayload(projectId, draft?: true)`, `redactedTicketPublishedPayload(projectId)`, `isRedactedTicketPublished(env)`.
- **Produces** (server): `NUMBERING_ROWS_SQL` (the one predicate string both key queries share); the columns `proj_tickets.draft_author_id`, `proj_tickets.draft_at`, `proj_tickets.draft_discarded`, `proj_visibility.draft_author_id` (written by T3); the SQL functions `purge_ledger` and `events_append_only` as redefined here.
- **Consumed by** T3 (columns), T5 (`discardDraft` calls `purge_ledger`, which redacts a draft's creation with the `draft` marker).

**Why the redaction needs a marker, and why `ticket.published` must survive.** The key is the position among numbering rows (a non-draft `ticket.created`, or any `ticket.published`). Two purge failures follow if the migration is not changed (spec §6.3):
1. A purged UNPUBLISHED draft keeps a redacted `ticket.created` that no longer says `draft: true`, so the key query COUNTS it: a number consumed by something that never had one. Cases 28.023 and 28.025.
2. A purged PUBLISHED draft-born ticket loses its `ticket.published` row (the old function deletes everything but `ticket.created`), so every later ticket in the project moves down by one: a number reused. Case 28.024.

**Why `replayRemaining` makes the TypeScript half necessary.** `purgeItem` replays the set's remaining ledger rows through every projection (`purge/erasure.ts:146-163`). After this task those rows include a redacted `ticket.published`, whose payload `{projectId, purged: true}` no longer satisfies the strict `ticketPublishedPayload`. Every reader that asks `isRedactedTicketCreated` first must ask the new predicate too, or `replayRemaining` throws inside the purge transaction. The readers today are `ticket-state.ts:136,509`, `projections/tickets.ts:566`; `proj-visibility.ts:243` and `rollups.ts` get a `ticket.published` arm in T3 and carry the guard there.

  const published = (base: Base, id: string, projectId: string): LedgerEvent =>

  async function legacyRows(workspaceId: string): Promise<Array<{ ticketId: string; projectId: string; number: number }>> {

         SELECT entity_id AS ticket_id,

           FROM events
          WHERE workspace_id = $1 AND type = 'ticket.created'

  import type { PoolClient } from 'pg';
  import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
  import { newUlid, type LedgerEvent } from '@gisik-nokma/domain';
  import { ticketNumbers } from '../../src/read/ticket-numbers.js';
  import { resetEntitySeqs } from '../helpers/apply.js';
  import { createTestDatabase, type TestDatabase } from '../helpers/db.js';
  import { appendTestEvent } from '../helpers/ledger.js';
  import { ev, seedWorkspace, ticketCreated, TYPE_ID, type Base } from './world.js';

  let db: TestDatabase;
  beforeAll(async () => {
    db = await createTestDatabase();
    resetEntitySeqs();
  }, 60_000);
  afterAll(async () => {
    await db.drop();
  });

  const draftCreated = (base: Base, id: string, projectId: string): LedgerEvent =>
    ev(base, 'ticket', id, 'ticket.created', { typeId: TYPE_ID, projectId, parentId: null, title: 'd', start: 'backlog', draft: true });
  const published = (base: Base, id: string, projectId: string): LedgerEvent =>
    ev(base, 'ticket', id, 'ticket.published', { projectId });
  async function append(...events: LedgerEvent[]): Promise<void> {
    for (const event of events) await appendTestEvent(db.pool, event);
  }
  /** The sanctioned purge path, ledger half only: `purge_ledger` is the one function the trigger admits. */
  async function purgeLedger(ticketId: string): Promise<void> {
    const client = await db.pool.connect();
    try {
      await client.query('BEGIN');
      await client.query('SELECT * FROM purge_ledger($1, $2)', ['ticket', ticketId]);
      await client.query('COMMIT');
    } catch (error) {
      await client.query('ROLLBACK');
      throw error;
    } finally {
      client.release();
    }
  }
  async function inTx<T>(fn: (client: PoolClient) => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
    const client = await db.pool.connect();
    try {
      await client.query('BEGIN');
      return await fn(client);
    } finally {
      await client.query('ROLLBACK').catch(() => {});
      client.release();
    }
  }
  const payloadOf = async (client: PoolClient | typeof db.pool, id: string, type: string): Promise<unknown> =>
    (await client.query('SELECT payload FROM events WHERE entity_id = $1 AND type = $2', [id, type])).rows[0]?.payload;

  describe('28.022 a discarded draft leaves no gap', () => {
    it('28.022 D1 (draft), T2, discard D1, T3: T2 is #1 and T3 is #2', async () => {
      const base = await seedWorkspace(db.pool);
      const P = newUlid();
      const [D1, T2, T3] = [newUlid(), newUlid(), newUlid()] as const;
      await append(draftCreated(base, D1, P), ticketCreated(base, T2, P, 'two'));
      await purgeLedger(D1); // the discard's ledger half
      await append(ticketCreated(base, T3, P, 'three'));
      const numbers = await ticketNumbers(db.pool, base.WS, [D1, T2, T3]);
      expect([numbers.get(D1), numbers.get(T2), numbers.get(T3)]).toEqual([undefined, 1, 2]);
      expect(await payloadOf(db.pool, D1, 'ticket.created')).toEqual({ projectId: P, purged: true, draft: true });
    });
  });

  describe('28.023 purge failure (1): an unpublished draft consumes no number when purged', () => {
    it('28.023 the redacted creation still says draft, so a later ticket keeps its number', async () => {
      const base = await seedWorkspace(db.pool);
      const P = newUlid();
      const [A, D, Z] = [newUlid(), newUlid(), newUlid()] as const;
      await append(ticketCreated(base, A, P, 'a'), draftCreated(base, D, P));
      await append(ticketCreated(base, Z, P, 'z'));
      const before = (await ticketNumbers(db.pool, base.WS, [Z])).get(Z);
      expect(before).toBe(2);
      await purgeLedger(D);
      expect((await ticketNumbers(db.pool, base.WS, [Z])).get(Z)).toBe(2);
      // control: a NON-draft ticket purged keeps its slot, so the next one moves by nothing either
      await purgeLedger(A);
      expect((await ticketNumbers(db.pool, base.WS, [A, Z])).get(A)).toBe(1);
      expect((await ticketNumbers(db.pool, base.WS, [Z])).get(Z)).toBe(2);

  describe('28.024 purge failure (2): a purged published draft keeps its slot', () => {
    it('28.024 the redacted ticket.published row is still a numbering row; later numbers do not shift', async () => {
      const base = await seedWorkspace(db.pool);
      const P = newUlid();
      const [A, X, B] = [newUlid(), newUlid(), newUlid()] as const;
      await append(ticketCreated(base, A, P, 'a'), draftCreated(base, X, P), ticketCreated(base, B, P, 'b'));
      await append(published(base, X, P));
      const before = await ticketNumbers(db.pool, base.WS, [A, X, B]);
      expect([before.get(A), before.get(B), before.get(X)]).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
      await purgeLedger(X);
      const after = await ticketNumbers(db.pool, base.WS, [A, X, B]);
      expect([after.get(A), after.get(B), after.get(X)]).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
      expect(await payloadOf(db.pool, X, 'ticket.published')).toEqual({ projectId: P, purged: true });
      expect(await payloadOf(db.pool, X, 'ticket.created')).toEqual({ projectId: P, purged: true, draft: true });
    });
  });

  describe('28.025 the trigger admits exactly three redactions', () => {
    it('28.025 the three exact shapes pass; every near miss and every outside-purge write is refused', async () => {
      const base = await seedWorkspace(db.pool);
      const P = newUlid();
      const [N, D, X, F] = [newUlid(), newUlid(), newUlid(), newUlid()] as const;
      await append(
        ticketCreated(base, N, P, 'plain'),
        draftCreated(base, D, P),
        draftCreated(base, X, P),
        published(base, X, P),
        ev(base, 'ticket', F, 'ticket.created', { typeId: TYPE_ID, projectId: P, parentId: null, title: 'f' }),
        ev(base, 'ticket', F, 'ticket.field_set', { fieldId: 'title', value: 'g' }),
      );
      const REFUSED = (op: string) => `events is append-only: ${op} refused`;
      /**
       * Opens a real purge of `id` (so the sanction is open and `purge_ledger` has put the row in its redacted
       * form), then tries to rewrite that row's payload. The trigger compares the new payload with the
       * redaction it computes from the row, so a rewrite to the same shape is accepted and any other is refused.
       * The whole transaction is rolled back, so the shared world is unchanged between probes.
       */
      const rewrite = (id: string, type: string, payload: object): Promise<string> =>
        inTx(async (client) => {
          await client.query('SELECT * FROM purge_ledger($1, $2)', ['ticket', id]);
          try {
            await client.query('UPDATE events SET payload = $3 WHERE entity_id = $1 AND type = $2', [id, type, JSON.stringify(payload)]);
            return 'accepted';
          } catch (error) {
            return (error as Error).message;
          }
        });
      // the three exact shapes: accepted
      expect(await rewrite(N, 'ticket.created', { projectId: P, purged: true })).toBe('accepted');
      expect(await rewrite(D, 'ticket.created', { projectId: P, purged: true, draft: true })).toBe('accepted');
      expect(await rewrite(X, 'ticket.published', { projectId: P, purged: true })).toBe('accepted');
      // near misses, each the same call with one input changed: refused
      expect(await rewrite(D, 'ticket.created', { projectId: P, purged: true })).toBe(REFUSED('UPDATE')); // marker dropped
      expect(await rewrite(N, 'ticket.created', { projectId: P, purged: true, draft: true })).toBe(REFUSED('UPDATE')); // marker invented
      expect(await rewrite(X, 'ticket.published', { projectId: P, purged: true, draft: true })).toBe(REFUSED('UPDATE'));
      expect(await rewrite(X, 'ticket.published', { projectId: P, purged: true, extra: 1 })).toBe(REFUSED('UPDATE'));
      expect(await rewrite(X, 'ticket.published', { projectId: newUlid(), purged: true })).toBe(REFUSED('UPDATE')); // another project
      // outside a purge every write is refused, whatever the type, with the original message
      for (const type of ['ticket.created', 'ticket.published', 'ticket.field_set']) {
        const id = type === 'ticket.published' ? X : type === 'ticket.field_set' ? F : N;
        await expect(db.pool.query('UPDATE events SET payload = $2 WHERE entity_id = $1 AND type = $3', [id, '{}', type])).rejects.toMatchObject({ message: REFUSED('UPDATE') });
        await expect(db.pool.query('DELETE FROM events WHERE entity_id = $1 AND type = $2', [id, type])).rejects.toMatchObject({ message: REFUSED('DELETE') });
      }
    });
  });

  -- Up Migration
  -- Drafts T2 (spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-03-drafts-design.md §4.1, §6.3, R19, R28).
  --
  -- 1. The draft flag, projected from TicketState.draft. NULL for every ticket that is not a draft
  --    (every existing row). `draft_author_id` is the audience mirror on proj_visibility (every
  --    v-joined read already has it) and the head state on proj_tickets (the engine and the t-joined
  --    reads have it). `draft_at` and `draft_discarded` exist so rowToTicketState can rebuild
  --    TicketState.draft exactly (the dual-client rig compares whole states with toEqual).
  ALTER TABLE proj_tickets
    ADD COLUMN draft_author_id text NULL,
    ADD COLUMN draft_at timestamptz NULL,
    ADD COLUMN draft_discarded boolean NULL;
  ALTER TABLE proj_visibility
    ADD COLUMN draft_author_id text NULL;

  -- Partial: drafts are the rare rows. The hot path is `draft_author_id IS NULL` (every view ANDs it), which
  -- an index on the non-null rows cannot serve; these indexes serve the author's own list and the sweep.
  CREATE INDEX proj_tickets_drafts_idx ON proj_tickets (workspace_id, draft_author_id) WHERE draft_author_id IS NOT NULL;
  CREATE INDEX proj_visibility_drafts_idx ON proj_visibility (workspace_id, draft_author_id) WHERE draft_author_id IS NOT NULL;

  COMMENT ON COLUMN proj_tickets.draft_author_id IS 'The author of a DRAFT ticket, or NULL. A draft is private to this user alone (owner, admins and the assignee included), has no key, and is on no board or list. Cleared by ticket.published. Drafts spec R17-R19.';
  COMMENT ON COLUMN proj_tickets.draft_at IS 'The serverTime of the ticket.created {draft:true} that made this a draft, or NULL.';
  COMMENT ON COLUMN proj_tickets.draft_discarded IS 'TRUE once the author has submitted ticket.discarded and the erasure has not yet landed (it is a crash window; the sweep finishes it). NULL for a draft not discarded and for every non-draft.';
  COMMENT ON COLUMN proj_visibility.draft_author_id IS 'Mirror of proj_tickets.draft_author_id, so the shared visibility predicates can close a draft without joining proj_tickets. NULL for every non-draft.';

  -- 2. purge_ledger keeps the NUMBERING ROWS (spec §6.3). A ticket's key is its position among its project's
  --    non-draft ticket.created rows plus its ticket.published rows. A purge redacts ticket.created to
  --    {projectId, purged: true} — plus draft: true when the original said so, so a purged unpublished draft
  --    is still NOT counted — and redacts ticket.published to {projectId, purged: true} instead of deleting
  --    it, so a purged published draft keeps its slot. Every other event of the set is deleted as before.
  CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION purge_ledger(p_kind text, p_id text)
  RETURNS TABLE (erased_kind text, erased_id text)
  LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp
  AS $$
  DECLARE
    v_key text := p_kind || ':' || p_id;
  BEGIN
    IF p_kind NOT IN ('workspace', 'project', 'ticket', 'note') THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'purge_ledger: unknown kind %', p_kind;
    END IF;
    DROP TABLE IF EXISTS pg_temp.purge_set;
    CREATE TEMP TABLE purge_set (
      set_kind  text NOT NULL,
      set_id    text NOT NULL,
      purge_key text NOT NULL,
      PRIMARY KEY (set_kind, set_id)
    ) ON COMMIT DROP;
    INSERT INTO pg_temp.purge_set (set_kind, set_id, purge_key)
      SELECT s.set_kind, s.set_id, v_key FROM purge_erasure_set(p_kind, p_id) s;
    PERFORM set_config('gisik.purge', v_key, true);
    IF p_kind IN ('ticket', 'note') THEN
      UPDATE events e
         SET payload = CASE
               WHEN e.type = 'ticket.created' AND e.payload->>'draft' = 'true'
                 THEN jsonb_build_object('projectId', e.payload->>'projectId', 'purged', true, 'draft', true)
               ELSE jsonb_build_object('projectId', e.payload->>'projectId', 'purged', true)
             END
        FROM pg_temp.purge_set s
       WHERE e.entity_kind = s.set_kind AND e.entity_id = s.set_id
         AND e.type IN ('ticket.created', 'ticket.published');
      DELETE FROM events e
       USING pg_temp.purge_set s
       WHERE e.entity_kind = s.set_kind AND e.entity_id = s.set_id
         AND e.type NOT IN ('ticket.created', 'ticket.published');
    ELSE
      DELETE FROM events e
       USING pg_temp.purge_set s
       WHERE e.entity_kind = s.set_kind AND e.entity_id = s.set_id;
    END IF;
    DELETE FROM snapshots sn
     USING pg_temp.purge_set s
     WHERE sn.entity_kind = s.set_kind AND sn.entity_id = s.set_id;
    RETURN QUERY SELECT s.set_kind, s.set_id FROM pg_temp.purge_set s ORDER BY s.set_kind, s.set_id;
  END;
  $$;
  REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION purge_ledger(text, text) FROM PUBLIC;

  -- 3. The append-only trigger admits exactly the three redactions and nothing else. The column-equality
  --    guard is the original's; only the payload test grew.

    v_key text;
    v_sanctioned boolean := false;
  BEGIN
    IF TG_OP = 'TRUNCATE' THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'events is append-only: % refused', TG_OP;
    END IF;
    v_key := current_setting('gisik.purge', true);
    IF v_key IS NOT NULL AND v_key <> '' AND to_regclass('pg_temp.purge_set') IS NOT NULL THEN
      EXECUTE 'SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_temp.purge_set WHERE set_kind = $1 AND set_id = $2 AND purge_key = $3)'
        INTO v_sanctioned

    END IF;
    IF NOT v_sanctioned THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'events is append-only: % refused', TG_OP;
    END IF;
    IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
      RETURN OLD;
    END IF;
    IF OLD.type IN ('ticket.created', 'ticket.published')
       AND NEW.payload = CASE
             WHEN OLD.type = 'ticket.created' AND OLD.payload->>'draft' = 'true'
               THEN jsonb_build_object('projectId', OLD.payload->>'projectId', 'purged', true, 'draft', true)
             ELSE jsonb_build_object('projectId', OLD.payload->>'projectId', 'purged', true)
           END
       AND (NEW.id, NEW.workspace_id, NEW.entity_kind, NEW.entity_id, NEW.type, NEW.version, NEW.actor_id,
            NEW.origin, NEW.client_time, NEW.server_time, NEW.seq, NEW.workspace_seq)
           IS NOT DISTINCT FROM
           (OLD.id, OLD.workspace_id, OLD.entity_kind, OLD.entity_id, OLD.type, OLD.version, OLD.actor_id,
            OLD.origin, OLD.client_time, OLD.server_time, OLD.seq, OLD.workspace_seq) THEN
      RETURN NEW;
    END IF;
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'events is append-only: % refused', TG_OP;
  END;
  $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

  /**

  `packages/domain/src/purge.ts`: replace `:27-40` with
  ```ts
  export function redactedTicketCreatedPayload(
    projectId: string,
    draft?: true,
  ): { projectId: string; purged: true; draft?: true } {
    // Drafts T2: a DRAFT's creation keeps its marker, so the key query (which does not count a draft's
    // creation) still does not count it after a purge. `purge_ledger` builds the same object in SQL.
    return draft === true ? { projectId, purged: true, draft: true } : { projectId, purged: true };
  }

  /**
   * A purged ticket's `ticket.published` is KEPT, redacted (drafts T2): it is a numbering row, and deleting it
   * would shift every later key in the project down by one.
   */
  export function redactedTicketPublishedPayload(projectId: string): { projectId: string; purged: true } {
    return { projectId, purged: true };
  }

  /** True exactly for a redacted `ticket.published` (`=== true`, for `isRedactedTicketCreated`'s reason). */
  export function isRedactedTicketPublished(env: Pick<EventEnvelope, 'type' | 'payload'>): boolean {
    if (env.type !== 'ticket.published') return false;
    const payload = env.payload;
    if (payload === null || typeof payload !== 'object') return false;
    return (payload as { purged?: unknown }).purged === true;
  }
  ```

**Interfaces:**
- **Consumes** (T1): `TicketState.draft`, `ticketCreatedPayload.draft`, `isRedactedTicketPublished` (T2). (T2): the four columns.
- **Produces:**
  - `ResolvedVisibility.draftAuthorId: string | null` (REQUIRED, so the compiler finds every literal) and the `canSeeResolved` / `canSee` answer `false` for a draft, for everyone;
  - `visibleTicketsWhere` and `LIVE_TICKET_WHERE` closed on `draft_author_id`; the new export `LIVE_BASE_WHERE` (the deleted and container halves alone; T9's `ticketIsOpenable` and the doors use it);
  - `seedTicket(pool, { …, draftBy })` (a draft: `start: 'backlog'`, `draft: true`, the head row carries `draft_author_id`);
  - `seedDraftWorld(pool, read): Promise<DraftWorld>` and `withDraftsOpened(pool, ids, run)` (test helpers, reused by T4 and T9).
- **Consumed by:** T4 (`canOpen` is `canSee || isOpenableDraft`; the doors turn the closure back on for the author), T5 (the same columns drive the engine's `getEntityState`), T9.

**What this task does to the author, stated so nobody is surprised.** After it the author is closed out of their own draft too: `canSee` is `false` for them, so G1 (`check-permission.ts:1639`) refuses their `ticket.field_set`, and no door lists the draft. That is the spec's design (the doors are T4) and the window exists only on the release branch. The cases here therefore never assert an author's 200; T4 owns every author-side expectation.

**One site the spec did not list, and the reason it is T5's.** The engine reads a parent's children through `getChildrenStatesFromDb` (`projections/tickets.ts:266`), which counts a DRAFT child as open work: `checks/close.ts:71` and `transition.ts:153` refuse to close a published parent over "N child tickets still open" where one of the N is a private draft nobody else can see, and the auto-close candidate query (`auto-close/sweep.ts:187-193`, "the two must answer alike") does the same. The rollup edit here (C1) fixes the displayed progress; the engine count and that `NOT EXISTS` change together, in T5, so the sweep and the engine keep answering alike. Until then a published parent with a draft child cannot be closed. Recorded in the final report as a spec gap.

**Why every `canSeeResolved` literal changes in this task.** `draftAuthorId` is required, not optional: an optional field would let a hand-built literal keep compiling and keep answering "visible" for a draft. Five literals break at compile time (`rollup.ts:337`, `restricted-parents.ts:100`, `legacy-rollup-for.ts:114`, `can-see.test.ts:80`, and `getResolvedVisibility`'s return); `can-read-note.ts:94,123` spreads `getResolvedVisibility`'s result and picks the field up with no edit.

    /** published, Backlog, assigned to `outsider`, child of the parent */
    twinId: string;
    /** published, `doing` since STALE_SINCE, due DUE, assigned to `outsider` */
    twinActiveId: string;
    /** draft by `member`, Backlog, assigned to `outsider`, child of the parent */
    draftId: string;
    /** draft by `member`, PLANTED in `doing` since STALE_SINCE, due DUE, assigned to `outsider`, child of the parent */
    draftActiveId: string;
    /** draft by `member`, PLANTED in `doing`, no parent, assigned to `member` (the author's own My Work) */
    rootDraftId: string;
    /** draft by `projectLead`, Backlog, explicit audience [guest] (planted) */
    guestDraftId: string;
    draftIds: readonly string[];
  };

  /**
   * Builds the world every closed-read case shares, on top of `buildReadTestApp`'s read world.
   *
   * Two of the drafts sit in `doing`. No door can produce that: a draft is born in the Backlog and
   * `ticket.transitioned` on a draft is refused (T5). They are planted with hand-built events, and that is the
   * point: a board and an Attention strip would omit a Backlog draft for an unrelated reason (the board has no
   * Backlog column), so only a draft in an ACTIVE state tests that the predicate, and not the state, is what
   * closes it. The same goes for `guestDraftId`'s explicit audience.
   */
  export async function seedDraftWorld(pool: Pool, read: ReadWorld): Promise<DraftWorld> {
    const { workspaceId, projectId, owner, member } = read.world;
    const outsider = read.userIds.outsider;
    const lead = read.userIds.projectLead;
    const guest = read.userIds.guest;
    const ids = {
      parentId: newUlid(), twinId: newUlid(), twinActiveId: newUlid(),
      draftId: newUlid(), draftActiveId: newUlid(), rootDraftId: newUlid(), guestDraftId: newUlid(),
    };
    const created = (actorId: string, id: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>): LedgerEvent =>
      makeCommitted({
        workspaceId, actorId, entity: { kind: 'ticket', id }, type: 'ticket.created',
        payload: { typeId: 'task', projectId, parentId: null, ...payload },
      });
    const toDoing = (actorId: string, id: string): LedgerEvent =>
      makeCommitted({
        workspaceId, actorId, entity: { kind: 'ticket', id }, type: 'ticket.transitioned',
        payload: { to: 'doing' }, clientTime: STALE_SINCE, serverTime: STALE_SINCE,
      });
    const due = (actorId: string, id: string): LedgerEvent =>
      makeCommitted({
        workspaceId, actorId, entity: { kind: 'ticket', id }, type: 'ticket.field_set',
        payload: { fieldId: 'dueDate', value: { date: DUE } },
      });
    const draft = { start: 'backlog', draft: true } as const;
    const events: LedgerEvent[] = [
      created(owner, ids.parentId, { typeId: 'epic', title: 'Quokka parent' }),
      created(owner, ids.twinId, { parentId: ids.parentId, title: TWIN_TITLE, assigneeId: outsider }),
      created(owner, ids.twinActiveId, { parentId: ids.parentId, title: 'Quokka twin active', assigneeId: outsider }),
      toDoing(owner, ids.twinActiveId),
      due(owner, ids.twinActiveId),
      created(member, ids.draftId, { parentId: ids.parentId, title: DRAFT_TITLE, assigneeId: outsider, ...draft }),
      created(member, ids.draftActiveId, { parentId: ids.parentId, title: `${DRAFT_TITLE} active`, assigneeId: outsider, ...draft }),
      toDoing(member, ids.draftActiveId),
      due(member, ids.draftActiveId),
      created(member, ids.rootDraftId, { title: `${DRAFT_TITLE} root`, assigneeId: member, ...draft }),
      toDoing(member, ids.rootDraftId),
      created(lead, ids.guestDraftId, { title: `${DRAFT_TITLE} for a guest`, ...draft }),
      makeCommitted({
        workspaceId, actorId: lead, entity: { kind: 'ticket', id: ids.guestDraftId }, type: 'visibility.set',
        payload: { ticketId: ids.guestDraftId, mode: 'explicit', userIds: [guest] },
      }),
    ];
    await applyCommitted(pool, events);
    return {
      ...ids,
      draftIds: [ids.draftId, ids.draftActiveId, ids.rootDraftId, ids.guestDraftId],
    };
  }

  /**
   * Runs `run` with the draft flag CLEARED on these tickets in both projections, then puts it back.
   *
   * This is the control of every closed-read case: the same request, by the same viewer, with the only thing
   * that differs being the flag. A closed read whose "absent" cannot be told from "the fixture never held it"
   * proves nothing.
   */
  export async function withDraftsOpened<T>(pool: Pool, ids: readonly string[], run: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
    const { rows } = await pool.query<{ ticket_id: string; draft_author_id: string }>(
      'SELECT ticket_id, draft_author_id FROM proj_tickets WHERE ticket_id = ANY($1::text[]) AND draft_author_id IS NOT NULL',
      [ids],
    );
    if (rows.length !== ids.length) {
      throw new Error(`withDraftsOpened: ${ids.length - rows.length} of these ${ids.length} tickets are not drafts`);
    }
    const set = async (value: (id: string) => string | null): Promise<void> => {
      for (const row of rows) {
        await pool.query('UPDATE proj_tickets SET draft_author_id = $2 WHERE ticket_id = $1', [row.ticket_id, value(row.ticket_id)]);
        await pool.query('UPDATE proj_visibility SET draft_author_id = $2 WHERE ticket_id = $1', [row.ticket_id, value(row.ticket_id)]);
      }
    };
    await set(() => null);
    try {
      return await run();
    } finally {
      const author = new Map(rows.map((row) => [row.ticket_id, row.draft_author_id]));
      await set((id) => author.get(id) ?? null);
    }
  }
  ```

  - `projections/tickets.ts`, `TicketRow` (after `deleted_by`, `:~114`):

      draft_author_id: string | null;
      draft_at: Date | null;

    ```
  - `rowToTicketState`, after the `deleted:` member (`:~239`), on `closed`'s rule (both columns agree there is a draft, or there is none) and with the key ABSENT on a non-draft, as the reducer leaves it:
    ```ts
        // ABSENT on every non-draft, never `undefined`-valued and never null: the reducer writes no `draft` key
        // for a published ticket and `ticket.published` removes it, and the dual-client rig compares whole
        // states with `toEqual` (28.045). `draft_at` is `timestamptz` against an ISO string, so the null arm is
        // spelled out as `reopened_at`'s is.
        ...(row.draft_author_id === null || row.draft_at === null
          ? {}
          : {
              draft: {
                authorId: row.draft_author_id,
                at: row.draft_at.toISOString(),
                ...(row.draft_discarded === true ? { discarded: true as const } : {}),
              },
            }),

The `DO UPDATE` list is what makes `ticket.published` CLEAR an existing row (the same reason `deleted_at` is in it), so it is not optional:

          next.draft?.authorId ?? null,
          next.draft?.at ?? null,

            );
            return;
          }

  ```ts
  type Probe = { role: ReadRole; url: string; marker: string };

  async function body(role: ReadRole, url: string): Promise<string> {
    const response = await read.app.inject({ method: 'GET', url, headers: read.authOf(role) });
    expect(response.statusCode, `${role} ${url}: ${response.body}`).toBe(200);
    return response.body;
  }

  /**
   * The shape of every closed-read case: the draft's marker is ABSENT from the answer, and the SAME request by
   * the SAME viewer with only the flag cleared CARRIES it. The second half is the haystack control: an absence
   * that cannot be told from "the fixture never held it", or from the route paging it out, proves nothing.
   */
  async function expectClosed(probes: readonly Probe[]): Promise<void> {
    for (const { role, url, marker } of probes) {
      const closed = await body(role, url);
      expect(closed, `${role} ${url}: the draft ${marker} is in the answer`).not.toContain(marker);
      const opened = await withDraftsOpened(db.pool, world.draftIds, () => body(role, url));
      expect(opened, `${role} ${url}: the control does not show ${marker}`).toContain(marker);
    }
  }
  const PEOPLE: readonly ReadRole[] = ['owner', 'admin', 'member', 'outsider'];
  const eachPerson = (url: string, marker: string): Probe[] => PEOPLE.map((role) => ({ role, url, marker }));
  const PROJECT = (): string => read.world.projectId;
  const WS = (): string => read.world.workspaceId;

  describe('28.051 the board', () => {
    it('never carries a draft, one planted in an active state included', async () => {
      await expectClosed(eachPerson(`/v1/projects/${PROJECT()}/board`, world.draftActiveId));

    await seedTicket(db.pool, { workspaceId: ws, projectId: theirs, ticketId: openToAll });

    await applyAll(db.pool, [setVisibilityEnv(ws, otherDraft, 'explicit', [author])]);

    const opener = await record(ticketEvent(ws, 'comment.added', openToAll, { body: 'still readable' }, viewer));

      type: 'membership.granted', payload: { userId: viewer, role: 'member' }, actorId: newUlid(),

    expect(ids).toContain(`purge:${explicitElsewhere}`); // CONTROL: the list is real and itemised
    expect(ids).not.toContain(`purge:${otherDraft}`);     // an id the recipient stands in no relationship to
    await db.pool.query('UPDATE proj_visibility SET draft_author_id = NULL WHERE ticket_id = $1', [otherDraft]);
    expect(idsOf(await collect(viewer, ws, opener.workspaceSeq - 1))).toContain(`purge:${otherDraft}`);
  });

- [ ] **Step 6: The census (28.050)**

  This is the test that makes Review Focus 1 hold for sites nobody has written yet. It parses every file of `apps/server/src` with the TypeScript compiler API (`typescript` is already a devDependency of `apps/server`; `test/integration/client-contract.test.ts:3` imports it the same way) and counts, per file, five kinds of site: a string or template literal holding SQL that names `proj_tickets`, one naming `proj_visibility` (anchored on `FROM|JOIN|INTO|UPDATE`, so prose and error strings that merely mention a table are not counted), and calls to `canSee(`, `canSeeResolved(`, `getResolvedVisibility(`. Each file with a non-zero count must be in the table below with its groups and the reason, and the counts must match; a new file, a moved count or a deleted site fails the run and prints the line to paste. It counts per file, not per line, so an unrelated edit above a site does not break it.

  The groups are the spec's (§4.2): **A** the predicates, **B** closed by A with no edit, **C** edited because it bypasses both predicates, **D** the doors that admit the author (T4), and **E**, which this plan adds, for code with no viewer in scope: projections, the engine's by-id reads, purge, maintenance. A site that serves a viewer belongs to A to D; E needs a one-line reason that says why no viewer is involved.

  **The table below was measured on `ec72d1f8` after this task's own edits** (40 files). Typed-links T2 to T5 and the KG series land before this plan runs and add readers (link reads, graph neighbours, reference lookups). **First action of this step on the new branch: write the test file with an EMPTY `CENSUS`, run it, and paste the printed lines into the table;** then classify each new line against §4.2 (spec A's link reads and spec C's graph reads are group B when they go through `visibleTicketsWhere` / `canSee`, group C if they read the tables raw), and re-read each moved row before trusting its reason.

  ```ts
  import { readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
  import { join, relative } from 'node:path';
  import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
  import * as ts from 'typescript';
  import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

  type Group = 'A' | 'B' | 'C' | 'D' | 'E';
  type Counts = { tickets: number; visibility: number; canSee: number; resolved: number; getResolved: number };
  type Site = Counts & { groups: readonly Group[]; why: string };

  const SRC = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../src', import.meta.url));
  const SQL = (table: string): RegExp => new RegExp(`\\b(FROM|JOIN|INTO|UPDATE)\\s+${table}\\b`, 'i');

  /** The five counts of one source text. Template expressions are not descended into (a nested literal is one site). */
  export function countSites(text: string, fileName = 'x.ts'): Counts {
    const sf = ts.createSourceFile(fileName, text, ts.ScriptTarget.Latest, true);
    const counts: Counts = { tickets: 0, visibility: 0, canSee: 0, resolved: 0, getResolved: 0 };
    const visit = (n: ts.Node): void => {
      if (ts.isStringLiteral(n) || ts.isNoSubstitutionTemplateLiteral(n) || ts.isTemplateExpression(n)) {
        const t = n.getText(sf);
        if (SQL('proj_tickets').test(t)) counts.tickets += 1;
        if (SQL('proj_visibility').test(t)) counts.visibility += 1;
        if (ts.isTemplateExpression(n)) return;
      }
      if (ts.isCallExpression(n) && ts.isIdentifier(n.expression)) {
        if (n.expression.text === 'canSee') counts.canSee += 1;
        if (n.expression.text === 'canSeeResolved') counts.resolved += 1;
        if (n.expression.text === 'getResolvedVisibility') counts.getResolved += 1;
      }
      ts.forEachChild(n, visit);
    };
    visit(sf);
    return counts;
  }

  const total = (c: Counts): number => c.tickets + c.visibility + c.canSee + c.resolved + c.getResolved;
  const line = (file: string, c: Counts): string =>
    `'${file}': { tickets: ${c.tickets}, visibility: ${c.visibility}, canSee: ${c.canSee}, resolved: ${c.resolved}, getResolved: ${c.getResolved}, groups: [], why: '' },`;

  function scanSource(): Record<string, Counts> {
    const out: Record<string, Counts> = {};
    const walk = (dir: string): void => {
      for (const name of readdirSync(dir)) {
        const path = join(dir, name);
        if (statSync(path).isDirectory()) walk(path);
        else if (path.endsWith('.ts')) {
          const c = countSites(readFileSync(path, 'utf8'), path);
          if (total(c) > 0) out[relative(SRC, path)] = c;
        }
      }
    };
    walk(SRC);
    return out;
  }

  /** What is wrong between the table and the source, one line each (empty when they agree). */
  export function problems(table: Record<string, Counts>, scanned: Record<string, Counts>): string[] {
    const out: string[] = [];
    for (const [file, c] of Object.entries(scanned)) {
      const listed = table[file];
      if (listed === undefined) out.push(`UNLISTED ${line(file, c)}`);
      else if (JSON.stringify([listed.tickets, listed.visibility, listed.canSee, listed.resolved, listed.getResolved]) !== JSON.stringify([c.tickets, c.visibility, c.canSee, c.resolved, c.getResolved])) {
        out.push(`MOVED ${line(file, c)}  (table says ${JSON.stringify([listed.tickets, listed.visibility, listed.canSee, listed.resolved, listed.getResolved])})`);
      }
    }
    for (const file of Object.keys(table)) if (scanned[file] === undefined) out.push(`STALE ${file} has no site any more: delete its row`);
    return out;
  }

  const CENSUS: Record<string, Site> = {
    'auto-close/sweep.ts': { tickets: 1, visibility: 0, canSee: 0, resolved: 0, getResolved: 0, groups: ['B', 'C'], why: "the candidate query ANDs LIVE_TICKET_WHERE; C7 adds 'ticket.published' to the entered-state read (:181); the NOT EXISTS child clause moves in T5" },

**Two decisions the code forced, stated so a reviewer does not reopen them.**
1. **`ticketAccess` asks `canSee` first.** `canSee` is `false` for every draft, so a published ticket costs exactly what it cost before and only a not-visible answer pays one extra `proj_tickets` read (the same economy `canSee` itself uses for the assignee arm, `visibility/can-see.ts:289-292`).
2. **G7 carries no new `draft: true` field.** `readTicket` already returns `ticketState: state` (`routes/tickets.ts:701-710`), and after T3 `state.draft` is the head state the reducer folds, so the response says `ticketState.draft = { authorId, at }` and `key: null` (T2: a draft has no numbering row). T8 maps `TicketRead.draft` from `ticketState.draft !== undefined`; a second field would be a second claim that can disagree.

**What the author can do after this task, and what is still T5's.** The author can edit their draft over HTTP (G1 admits the allowlist, refuses the rest with `draft.not-allowed`), receive its events on every device, and read it. The ENGINE still knows nothing about drafts: a hand-built `ticket.reparented` naming another person's draft as parent is judged by the old rules (R3 and R4 are T5), and `ticket.published` and `ticket.discarded` are accepted by the permission gate but nothing publishes or erases (T5). None of that is reachable from a UI before T8. A `note.attached` naming a draft is still refused for the author (`check-permission.ts:1585` stays `canSee` until T9, G11), and the attachment routes stay closed for the author until T9 (G10).

  describe('28.071 G1: the author\'s permission gate on a draft', () => {
    async function world() {
      const { workspaceId, projectId } = await workspace();
      const author = newUlid();
      const owner = newUlid();
      const admin = newUlid();
      const assignee = newUlid();
      await seedMember(db.pool, workspaceId, owner, 'owner');
      await seedMember(db.pool, workspaceId, admin, 'admin');
      await seedMember(db.pool, workspaceId, author, 'member');
      await seedMember(db.pool, workspaceId, assignee, 'member');
      const draftId = newUlid();
      const publishedId = newUlid();
      await seedTicket(db.pool, { workspaceId, projectId, ticketId: draftId, draftBy: author, birthAssigneeId: assignee });
      await seedTicket(db.pool, { workspaceId, projectId, ticketId: publishedId, createdBy: author });
      return { workspaceId, author, owner, admin, assignee, draftId, publishedId };
    }
    const REFUSED = [
      'ticket.transitioned', 'ticket.closed', 'ticket.reopened', 'ticket.ranked',
      'comment.added', 'ticket.collaborator_added', 'visibility.set', 'ticket.deleted',
    ] as const;

    it('admits the allowlist for the author, refuses the rest with draft.not-allowed, and answers everyone else as an unknown ticket', async () => {
      const w = await world();
      const as = (type: string, ticketId: string, actorId: string, payload: unknown = {}) => {
        const env = type === 'visibility.set'
          ? setVisibilityEnv(w.workspaceId, ticketId, 'workspace', undefined, actorId)
          : ticketEvent(w.workspaceId, type, ticketId, actorId, payload);
        return gate(env, actorId);
      };

      for (const type of DRAFT_ALLOWED_EVENT_TYPES) {
        expect(await as(type, w.draftId, w.author), type).toBeNull();
      }
      for (const type of REFUSED) {
        expect(await as(type, w.draftId, w.author), type).toEqual({
          refused: true,
          rule: DRAFT_NOT_ALLOWED_RULE,
          reason: draftNotAllowedReason(type),
        });
      }
      expect(draftNotAllowedReason('ticket.deleted')).toBe('A draft cannot be deleted. Discard it instead.');

      // everyone else, owner and admin and the assignee included: the answer an unknown ticket gets
      const unknown = await as('ticket.field_set', newUlid(), w.owner, { fieldId: 'title', value: 'x' });
      expect(unknown).toEqual({ refused: true, rule: PERMISSION_VISIBILITY_RULE, reason: TICKET_NOT_VISIBLE_REASON });
      for (const actor of [w.owner, w.admin, w.assignee]) {
        for (const type of ['ticket.field_set', 'ticket.discarded', 'ticket.closed'] as const) {
          expect(await as(type, w.draftId, actor, { fieldId: 'title', value: 'x' }), `${actor} ${type}`).toEqual(unknown);
        }
      }

      // CONTROL, same `it`: the SAME author's `ticket.closed`, refused above on the draft, is admitted on a published ticket
      expect(await as('ticket.closed', w.publishedId, w.author)).toBeNull();
    });
  });

      // the lead's device: the mirror image
      expect(await reconcile('projectLead', held)).toEqual(sorted([world.draftId, world.rootDraftId]));

      for (const role of ['owner', 'admin', 'outsider'] as const) {

  ```ts
  import type { Queryable } from '../db/queryable.js';
  import { resolveEffectiveRole, type EffectiveRole } from '../permissions/effective-role.js';
  import { canSee } from './can-see.js';

  /**
   * What a person may do with a ticket id (drafts spec §4.2, group D). The three answers are the three
   * things a door can say: `visible` (an ordinary reader, `canSee`), `own-draft` (the author of a draft they
   * can still create in), `none` (the unknown-ticket answer, for everyone else).
   */
  export type TicketAccess = 'visible' | 'own-draft' | 'none';

  /**
   * R18: an author reaches their draft only while they could still CREATE in its project, which is the test
   * `checkVisibilityPermission` makes for `ticket.created` (`ctx.eff.projects.has(projectId)`) plus a role that
   * may create at all. A guest, a revoked member, or a project the author is no longer on: closed, not erased.
   */
  export function holdsDraftRights(eff: EffectiveRole, projectId: string): boolean {
    const role = eff.workspaceRole;
    return (role === 'owner' || role === 'admin' || role === 'member') && eff.projects.has(projectId);
  }

  type DraftHead = {
    workspace_id: string;
    project_id: string;
    draft_author_id: string | null;
    draft_discarded: boolean | null;
  };

  /**
   * True when this ticket is a draft that `userId` authored, that is not flagged discarded, and that its author
   * may still open (R18). The workspace is the TICKET's own, never the caller's (`canSee`'s rule): a role held in
   * workspace A answers nothing about a draft in workspace B.
   */
  export async function isOpenableDraft(db: Queryable, userId: string, ticketId: string): Promise<boolean> {
    const { rows } = await db.query<DraftHead>(
      'SELECT workspace_id, project_id, draft_author_id, draft_discarded FROM proj_tickets WHERE ticket_id = $1',
      [ticketId],
    );
    const head = rows[0];
    if (head === undefined || head.draft_author_id !== userId || head.draft_discarded === true) return false;
    return holdsDraftRights(await resolveEffectiveRole(db, userId, head.workspace_id), head.project_id);
  }

  /**
   * `canSee` FIRST, so a published ticket costs exactly what it cost before; only a not-visible answer pays the
   * one extra read (the economy `canSee` itself uses for the assignee arm). `canSee` is false for every draft,
   * so `visible` is never returned for one while the flag is set.
   */
  export async function ticketAccess(db: Queryable, userId: string, ticketId: string): Promise<TicketAccess> {
    if (await canSee(db, userId, ticketId)) return 'visible';
    return (await isOpenableDraft(db, userId, ticketId)) ? 'own-draft' : 'none';
  }

  /** The door predicate: `canSee || isOpenableDraft`. Every door of group D calls this or `ticketAccess`. */
  export async function canOpen(db: Queryable, userId: string, ticketId: string): Promise<boolean> {
    return (await ticketAccess(db, userId, ticketId)) !== 'none';
  }
  ```

  import type { TicketState } from '@gisik-nokma/domain';
  import type { Queryable } from '../db/queryable.js';
  import { resolveEffectiveRole } from '../permissions/effective-role.js';
  import { holdsDraftRights } from '../visibility/can-open.js';
  import { visibleProjects } from './visible-projects.js';

  /** One row of the Drafts page and of `list_my_drafts`. It never carries a key: a draft has none (T2). */
  export type DraftListItem = {
    ticketId: string;
    projectId: string;
    projectName: string;
    typeId: string;
    title: string;
    parentId: string | null;
    /** The server instant of the draft's last ledger event (its creation when nothing followed). */
    updatedAt: string;
    /** `attachments` rows uploaded to THIS draft (R60); a sub-draft's are counted on the sub-draft. */
    attachmentCount: number;
  };

  type Row = {
    ticket_id: string;
    project_id: string;
    type_id: string;
    parent_id: string | null;
    fields: TicketState['fields'];
    updated_at: Date;
    attachment_count: string;
  };

  /**
   * The caller's own drafts in one workspace, newest first (drafts spec §12.2, R55). This is the ONE reader of
   * "my drafts": the Drafts page, `GET /v1/me/drafts`, the full bootstrap (G4) and the graph series call it.
   *
   * The filter is the flag and the viewer, not the audience: `draft_author_id = $2`, not discarded, and R18's
   * test through `holdsDraftRights`, which is the same function `isOpenableDraft` calls, so the list and the
   * doors cannot disagree about who still owns a draft. A project whose name the caller may not be told is
   * skipped (an author who can open a draft is on its project, so in practice nothing is).
   */
  export async function listMyDrafts(
    db: Queryable,
    userId: string,
    workspaceId: string,
    opts: { projectId?: string } = {},
  ): Promise<DraftListItem[]> {
    const eff = await resolveEffectiveRole(db, userId, workspaceId);
    if (eff.workspaceRole === null) return [];
    const { rows } = await db.query<Row>(
      `SELECT t.ticket_id, t.project_id, t.type_id, t.parent_id, t.fields,
              COALESCE(
                (SELECT max(e.server_time) FROM events e WHERE e.entity_kind = 'ticket' AND e.entity_id = t.ticket_id),
                t.draft_at
              ) AS updated_at,
              (SELECT count(*) FROM attachments a WHERE a.ticket_id = t.ticket_id) AS attachment_count
         FROM proj_tickets t
        WHERE t.workspace_id = $1 AND t.draft_author_id = $2 AND t.draft_discarded IS NOT TRUE
        ORDER BY updated_at DESC, t.ticket_id DESC`,
      [workspaceId, userId],
    );
    const names = new Map((await visibleProjects(db, eff, workspaceId)).map((p) => [p.projectId, p.name] as const));
    const items: DraftListItem[] = [];
    for (const row of rows) {
      if (opts.projectId !== undefined && row.project_id !== opts.projectId) continue;
      if (!holdsDraftRights(eff, row.project_id)) continue;
      const projectName = names.get(row.project_id);
      if (projectName === undefined) continue;
      const title = row.fields['title']?.value;
      items.push({
        ticketId: row.ticket_id,
        projectId: row.project_id,
        projectName,
        typeId: row.type_id,
        title: typeof title === 'string' ? title : '',
        parentId: row.parent_id,
        updatedAt: row.updated_at.toISOString(),
        attachmentCount: Number(row.attachment_count),
      });
    }
    return items;
  }
  ```

  ```ts
  import type { FastifyInstance, preHandlerHookHandler } from 'fastify';
  import type { Queryable } from '../db/queryable.js';
  import { READ_NOT_FOUND_BODY, requireMember } from '../read/membership.js';
  import { listMyDrafts, type DraftListItem } from '../read/drafts.js';

  /**
   * G8 (drafts spec §4.2): the two reads of "my drafts". The subject is the SESSION user and there is no
   * parameter that names another (`routes/my-work.ts`'s rule): a route that offered one would be a read of
   * someone else's private drafts behind a 200.
   */
  export function registerDraftRoutes(
    app: FastifyInstance,
    deps: { pool: Queryable },
    requireSession: preHandlerHookHandler,
  ): void {
    app.get<{ Params: { workspaceId: string } }>(
      '/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/drafts',
      { preHandler: requireSession },
      async (request, reply) => {
        const { workspaceId } = request.params;
        if ((await requireMember(deps.pool, request.currentUserId, workspaceId)) === null) {
          return reply.code(404).send(READ_NOT_FOUND_BODY);
        }
        return { items: await listMyDrafts(deps.pool, request.currentUserId, workspaceId) };
      },
    );

    // Every workspace the caller belongs to, like `GET /v1/me/deleted-items` (`routes/deleted-items.ts:15`):
    // MCP's `list_my_drafts` pages over this list (T7).
    app.get<{ Querystring: { workspaceId?: string; projectId?: string } }>(
      '/v1/me/drafts',
      { preHandler: requireSession },
      async (request) => {
        const userId = request.currentUserId;
        const { workspaceId, projectId } = request.query;
        const { rows } = await deps.pool.query<{ workspace_id: string }>(
          `SELECT m.workspace_id
             FROM proj_memberships m
             LEFT JOIN proj_workspaces pw ON pw.workspace_id = m.workspace_id
            WHERE m.user_id = $1 AND m.scope_kind = 'workspace' AND pw.deleted_at IS NULL
            ORDER BY m.workspace_id`,
          [userId],
        );
        const items: Array<DraftListItem & { workspaceId: string }> = [];
        for (const row of rows) {
          if (workspaceId !== undefined && row.workspace_id !== workspaceId) continue;
          const drafts = await listMyDrafts(deps.pool, userId, row.workspace_id, projectId === undefined ? {} : { projectId });
          for (const draft of drafts) items.push({ ...draft, workspaceId: row.workspace_id });
        }
        items.sort((a, b) =>
          a.updatedAt === b.updatedAt ? (a.ticketId < b.ticketId ? 1 : -1) : a.updatedAt < b.updatedAt ? 1 : -1,
        );
        return { items };
      },
    );
  }
